# 01-prepare-and-upgrade-webapp: Prepare and upgrade the WebApp project

Verify the .NET 11 SDK/toolchain and any global.json configuration, then upgrade the solution's single SDK-style ASP.NET Core project in one atomic pass. For `WebApp/WebApp.csproj`, retarget from net10.0 to net11.0 and update the 3 recommended NuGet packages: AutoMapper, Microsoft.EntityFrameworkCore.SqlServer, and Microsoft.EntityFrameworkCore.Tools. Keep package updates and API/source fixes within this task.

The assessment identifies 48+ affected locations, with 47 behavioral-change API notices and 1 binary-incompatible API finding. Review the assessment's API details and source incidents rather than converting behavioral notices into speculative fixes. Resolve the binary-incompatible API inline and apply only evidence-backed replacements for behavioral API references. Preserve application behavior and existing package compatibility for the 9 packages that require no upgrade.

**Done when**: The SDK/toolchain is net11-compatible, `WebApp/WebApp.csproj` targets net11.0, all recommended package updates are applied, the binary-incompatible API issue is resolved inline, the solution restores and builds with 0 errors, and the applicable existing tests pass.

## Research findings and execution reference

- Repository inventory confirmed one solution (`aspnet-core-api-boilerplate.sln`) and one SDK-style ASP.NET Core project (`WebApp/WebApp.csproj`) targeting `net10.0`; there are no project references or dependents, no test project, no `Directory.Build.props`, no `Directory.Packages.props`, no NuGet config, and no `global.json`.
- Toolchain check: `dotnet --info` reports SDK `11.0.100`, MSBuild `18.12.2`, and .NET 11 runtimes installed. `validate_dotnet_sdk_installation(net11.0)` reports a compatible SDK. `validate_dotnet_sdk_in_globaljson` reports no global.json to validate.
- Package discovery (`get_project_dependencies`) confirms non-CPM package references are defined directly in `WebApp/WebApp.csproj`. Update only these three to the assessment/tool-verified versions: `AutoMapper` 14.0.0 → 17.0.0; `Microsoft.EntityFrameworkCore.SqlServer` 10.0.2 → 11.0.0; `Microsoft.EntityFrameworkCore.Tools` 10.0.2 → 11.0.0. Preserve the existing `PrivateAssets` and `IncludeAssets` metadata for Tools.
- Keep the other nine package versions unchanged: Azure.Data.Tables 12.11.0; Azure.Extensions.AspNetCore.Configuration.Secrets 1.4.0; Azure.Identity 1.17.1; Azure.Storage.Blobs 12.27.0; Azure.Storage.Queues 12.25.0; Microsoft.ApplicationInsights.AspNetCore 2.23.0; Microsoft.Azure.Cosmos 3.56.0; Newtonsoft.Json 13.0.4; Swashbuckle.AspNetCore 10.1.0.
- Retarget the existing singular `<TargetFramework>` property to `net11.0`; do not introduce multi-targeting. The project is already SDK-style, so no conversion is needed.
- The required `Api.0001` incident is `OptionsConfigurationServiceCollectionExtensions.Configure<TOptions>(IServiceCollection, IConfiguration)` at `WebApp/Program.cs:22`. Its linked .NET guidance says configuration-binding APIs lost trim-preservation annotations and recommends the binding configuration source generator. `MySettings` is a public class with public settable properties, and the project currently has no generator-enabled setting. Enable `<EnableConfigurationBindingGenerator>true</EnableConfigurationBindingGenerator>` so the existing options binding call is intercepted by generated binding code; retain its existing section and service configuration to preserve behavior. This is the evidence-backed inline resolution.
- The 47 `Api.0003` behavioral notices group into four findings; do not make speculative API replacements:
  - 43 OpenAPI notices (`Produces` / `ProducesResponseType`) span `Controllers/{Cosmos,Sql,Table}/ProductsController.cs`, `FilesController.cs`, and `MessagesController.cs`. The .NET 11 documentation says multiple declarations for the same status on one operation are all retained in generated OpenAPI output. Inspection shows response attributes describe distinct status codes per action; no duplicate same-status declarations on a single action were found. No attribute changes are indicated. Documentation: https://learn.microsoft.com/aspnet/core/breaking-changes/11/openapi-multiple-produces-per-status?view=aspnetcore-11.0
  - One MemoryStream notice is `new MemoryStream()` in `Infrastructure/Cosmos/Models/MyCosmosJsonSerializer.cs:45`, used as a growing serialization buffer without explicit capacity assumptions. No code change is supported by the incident alone; verify serialization/build and record any remaining payload-size check if representative integration coverage is unavailable.
  - One exception-diagnostics notice is associated with `Program.cs:101` (`UseExceptionHandler("/error")`). The change applies when a registered `IExceptionHandler.TryHandleAsync` returns true. Repository search found no `IExceptionHandler` implementation/registration; the app uses the path overload and `ErrorController`. Also, the documented change was introduced in .NET 10, the current target. No replacement is indicated. Documentation: https://learn.microsoft.com/aspnet/core/breaking-changes/10/exception-handler-diagnostics-suppressed?view=aspnetcore-11.0
  - Two URI notices point to `new Uri(builder.Configuration["KeyVaultUrl"] ?? "")` in `Program.cs:20`. The documented removal of URI length limits was introduced in .NET 10, the current target; the configured Key Vault URL in `appsettings.json` is a conventional short absolute URL and no application validation relies on URI length limits. No replacement is indicated. Documentation: https://learn.microsoft.com/dotnet/core/compatibility/networking/10.0/uri-length-limits-removed
- There is no existing test project in the solution; tests are not applicable unless discovery/build reveals a test project. The project is SDK-style and has no legacy Windows-specific build requirements, so use `dotnet restore` and `dotnet build` for solution validation after the project/package/source changes.

## Behavioral API review

The four incident groups and their local triggers/dispositions are recorded above. The OpenAPI change is not triggered because no operation declares duplicate response metadata for the same status; URI and exception-diagnostics behavior changes predate this `net10.0` → `net11.0` upgrade and their documented triggers are absent; the MemoryStream use has no explicit capacity/exception-dependent behavior to replace. Build validation will confirm compilation, but no runtime endpoint/OpenAPI or Cosmos integration test project exists; a representative maximum-size Cosmos serialization check remains a focused follow-up only if production payload sizes approach a relevant capacity limit.

## Validation discoveries and evidence-backed adjustments

- The first solution build exposed the AutoMapper 17 constructor change at `Program.cs:60`: `MapperConfiguration` no longer accepts the one-argument form. The installed AutoMapper 17 package README demonstrates the `ILoggerFactory` constructor parameter. Register `IMapper` with a DI factory that passes the application's real `ILoggerFactory` to `MapperConfiguration`, retaining the existing `ShopProfile` and singleton `IMapper` lifetime while preserving AutoMapper diagnostics.
- The first restore/build also surfaced NU1903 for transitive `Microsoft.OpenApi` 2.3.0 (`GHSA-v5pm-xwqc-g5wc`). The advisory identifies 2.7.5 as the patched 2.x line; `Swashbuckle.AspNetCore.Swagger` 10.1.0 declares Microsoft.OpenApi 2.3.0 as its minimum dependency. Pin the transitive dependency to 2.7.5, retaining the compatible 2.x API and leaving all nine explicitly compatible direct package versions unchanged. Subsequent restore/build has zero warnings.
- AutoMapper's migration-skill lookup returned no matching skill. Its package-distributed README provides the constructor pattern used above; attempts to retrieve its hosted documentation failed at the network transport layer, so no additional claims are based on that unavailable source.
- Integrity review identified that an interim `NullLoggerFactory` implementation would suppress AutoMapper 17 license/runtime diagnostics. It was replaced with the application's DI-provided `ILoggerFactory`; re-run the affected solution build/test and obtain a fresh review verdict.

## Decomposition assessment

Loaded the .NET version-upgrade `Execution` stage and its always-applicable `breakdown-hints/common.md`. The common multi-project-ordering hint does not trigger (one project, no dependency graph); the large-package-replacement hint does not trigger (three version bumps, no package replacements). The selected All-at-Once strategy and TFM/package/API changes are one project migration with a single validation gate; request TaskBreaker assessment before source edits under the executor's project-scope escalation rule.
